title: Consumption ancestry attribution harvester and idempotent lineage sink
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a new "ancestry harvester" that consumes token and request telemetry to produce deterministic, lineage-aware billing attributions for per-route and per-tenant chargeback. The harvester reconstructs event ancestry (caller request -> gateway -> model route -> cache hits -> downstream retries) so we can attribute each token to the correct billing seat, apply reserved capacity discounts, and surface explainability metadata in the console. This ticket delivers the streaming enrichment, idempotent sink semantics, schema, and a canary/backfill plan.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end pipeline produces attribution records with stable lineage_id for 99.99% of requests
Reconciled daily ledger delta between new harvester and canonical ledger < 0.35% across top 100 tenants
Idempotent writes: repeated replays of the same Kafka partition range do not create duplicate charges
Backfill can be run for a 90-day window with bounded resource use and completes within SLA
Console shows per-route ancestry trace links for sample requests and cost breakdowns in staging
notes: 2026-02-21: Kickoff - scoped streaming-first approach to avoid multi-TB Spark backfills for incremental updates.
2026-02-25: Design review - agreed on DAG model (event -> parent_event_id chain) instead of full graph; reduces state size and supports constant-time ancestry reconstruction.

2026-03-01: Tech decision - use Flink (stateful low-latency processing) for the harvester consumer; output sink will be ClickHouse for fast console reads and BigQuery daily rollover for OLAP/backfill.
2026-03-04: Security review stubbed - PII gating required for user ids; added field-level encryption plan using KMS tokens and tokenization at the ingestion boundary.
2026-03-08: Implementation - core Flink job implemented (fingerprinting + parent join + weight calculation). Added murmur3_128 fingerprinting for event fingerprints to keep keys small and performant.
2026-03-10: PR feedback (infra): add tombstone handling for session end events and watemark-based late-arrival windowing to avoid double-count on retries.
2026-03-12: Canary prep - created canary topic config, test tenant list, and dashboard for delta monitoring vs existing ledger service.
engineering_tasks: Define canonical attribution schema and add versioning field (schema_v2)
Implement Flink consumer with idempotent fingerprint dedupe and parent-lookup cache
Add ClickHouse materialized table for near-real-time console queries (partitioned by org_id, date)
Build BigQuery daily rollup job and Parquet archival for cold storage
Implement field-level encryption for customer_id and end_user_id with KMS
Add unit and integration tests for late-arrival handling (watermarks, tombstones)
Create canary pipeline config and dashboards for delta / rate / cost metrics
Author runbook for backfill recovery and replay safety checks
qa_plan: Run synthetic traffic harness to exercise retry/replay scenarios; run reconciliation job comparing harvester output to canonical ledger for 30 days in staging; perform chaos tests (kafka partition loss, late events) and validate idempotency and tombstone handling.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy harvester in staging, run 7-day smoke with synthetic traffic. 2) Canary: route 1% of production tenant traffic (test tenants list) for 48 hours and monitor delta dashboards. 3) Expand to 25% if delta < 0.2% and no critical errors. 4) Full cutover with a coordinated 2-hour maintenance window; keep legacy ledger in read-only for 7 days before trimming.
backfill_strategy: Two-phase: (A) Bulk historical read via parquet export -> Spark idempotent loader writing to ClickHouse/BigQuery with fingerprint dedupe; (B) Incremental replays via Kafka for the last 30 days with windowed watermarking. Include throttling and checkpoints to avoid overloading ClickHouse.
open_questions: Should the lineage beacon include original client IP or just tokenized region? (privacy tradeoff)
Do we collapse retries into single attribution (winner-takes-all) or split costs across retries based on final token consumption?
What SLA do we guarantee for daily reconciliation job and who signs off on the 0.35% threshold?
